beats.new_visual_element: One hundred thousand genes, or twenty thousand
beats.narration: Here is the clearest one. The chapter says the DNA of the one hundred thousand genes is replicated during S phase. One hundred thousand is a pre-genome-project estimate from the nineteen nineties. The count from the NCBI gene database gives 19,116 known protein-coding genes, and the modern consensus sits near twenty thousand. The rest of that sentence is correct and stays.

beats.new_visual_element: UV does not make double-strand breaks
beats.narration: Two errors swap a mechanism for its neighbour. The chapter attributes double-strand breaks to ultraviolet stress. UV produces pyrimidine dimers and photoproducts, and between them that is essentially all UV photodamage. Neither is a double-strand break. It also calls CDKN1C maternally imprinted, which means the maternal copy is silenced. For CDKN1C only the maternal copy is expressed.

beats.act: THE CORRECTION TO MY OWN FINDING
beats.new_visual_element: A claim of mine that was too absolute
beats.narration: And here is the one I got wrong. My first pass recorded that approval for this class of inhibitor remains in breast cancer. A later pass caught it. Trilaciclib was approved in February 2021 for small cell lung cancer, in the same class, used to protect bone marrow rather than attack the tumour. Defensible if you only think about antitumour uses, and wrong as written.

props.costLine: The near-miss, not the invention. It happened to me the same way.

beats.narration: One more worth reporting against myself. The workbook says a trial was terminated early for futility. The registry says it completed. My conclusion that no phase three is active was right, and the status I repeated was not. Repeating a source's error while correcting a different one is its own failure mode.

beats.new_visual_element: The viewer gets the same job
beats.narration: So here is what I would hand to you. Take a document you trust and find one number in it that has a date attached, or should have. Then go and check whether anyone has measured it since. Most of what was wrong in this chapter was simply old, and nothing about reading it would tell you that.
